title: Maureen, grey nomad

greeting.text: The bell. A small woman in a quilted vest, carrying a paper plate under cling wrap as if it were the crown jewels.
Oh, thank goodness, a light on. I'm Maureen. I baked these at the van park in Tarrow this morning and I've nobody left to give them to. Go on, love. You look like you could use it.
She sets a scone on the counter and reads your name tag. "Sam. That's a good plain name." It takes you a second to realise she means you.

annoyed: Now, I don't mind a careful young person. But I am seventy-one, and I have been standing a while.

notes.wrist: She pays from a purse that shuts with a kiss-clasp. Skin like tissue paper. Every vein she owns is on show.
notes.reflection: In the mirror: a small bent back and a grey bun. It moves when she moves.
notes.shadow: Sensible shoes. One shadow, soft at the edges, tucked under her like a cat.

topics.answer: Forty-one years with Ken, then two without. The van's quieter now. Not better. He did all the reversing.
Mullane Flat, for the dahlia show. If they ever open the road. I've a tuber in the van fridge that won't keep forever.

topics.ask: That's very kind of you. Thank you.
topics.answer: Eat it while the cream's cold. That's all I ask.
topics.note: You don't. You smile, and you move the plate a little to one side.

topics.ask: Why are you being so nice to me?
topics.note: You find you don't have an answer ready.

topics.ask: What did Ken's hands look like?
topics.answer: ...Big. Freckled. A scar just here, from a bandsaw. What a thing to ask. What a thing to make me remember.

wren.arrive: Oh, here we go. Somebody's nan.
wren.adviceLine: I don't like her. Nobody is that nice at midnight. Tell her we're shut, Sam. Trust me on this one.

after.serve: Finally. I thought she was going to adopt you.
after.turnAway: Good. That's good. She'd only have kept you talking. ...I don't like sharing.
after.shelter: She's on the cot. She asked me whether you were eating enough. I said I'd see to it.

serve.text: Unleaded's on pump two. There's a lay-by past the canopy if you'd rather sit the fog out in the van.
You're a good one, Sam. Whoever taught you your manners did a proper job.
She pats your hand. Hers is warm. You notice the warmth, as if it were unusual.

turnAway.text: Oh. Oh, of course, I've kept you. You keep the scone, love.
She goes out backwards, apologising to the door.

shelter.text: The road isn't safe tonight. We've a cot out the back.
Well, if it's no trouble. I'll not sleep, mind. I'll just rest my eyes.

walkout.text: I think I've taken up enough of your evening, dear. I know when I'm being looked over.
She leaves the scone. She does not look back at it, or at you.

report.serve: A woman in a campervan sat out the fog in the lay-by at Corrigan's and has been in touch with her family. She asked us to pass on that the young one on nights should eat something.
report.turnAway: A campervan is parked at the Corrigan's pumps with its lights on and its side door open. There is a kettle boiled dry on the stove. Rangers would like to speak to the owner.
report.walkout: A campervan has been found in the run-off lane two kilometres below Corrigan's. Its owner, a woman in her seventies, was not inside. A tray of scones was.
report.shelter: A traveller who sheltered at Corrigan's overnight has rung her daughter. She says the staff were lovely. She says one of them stood outside her door until morning.
report.missed: A campervan waited at Corrigan's pumps for some time overnight and was not attended to. It is no longer there.
